operatingCostModel.summary: Treat student co-design, cloud/platform consumption and student-facing AI inference as continuing product operating costs rather than one-off Year One items. Paid student visioning and co-design remains £15,000 per year. Azure, environments and platform costs ramp £50,000 / £75,000 / £100,000 across mobilisation and then £100,000 per year in BAU. Student-facing AI inference, retrieval and token consumption uses the same £50,000 / £75,000 / £100,000 high-water ramp and £100,000 BAU allowance. James Costerton has sense-checked both ramps as reasonable high-water assumptions; the next task is to refine them from architecture, demand and unit-cost evidence rather than to treat them as unsupported placeholders. The AI allowance remains separate from the £90,000 Devin/Cognition engineering-productivity budget held in 4.1.3.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: £225,000 three-year high-water planning envelope using the same £50,000 / £75,000 / £100,000 ramp as platform costs, then £100,000 per year as a BAU high-water allowance. James Costerton considers this a reasonable high-water assumption. It is not yet a usage forecast: model mix, interactions per active student, context and retrieval design, caching, embeddings, safety, observability and any institutional AI gateway should progressively turn the allowance into a measured unit-cost model.
